transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-06-24 10:00 AM UTC | Duration: 62 minutes | Location: All-Hands (Zoom)
Attendees: Evelyn Park, Marcus Li, Priya Nair, Daniel Ruiz, Sophie Chen, Mateo Alvarez, Lina Kaur + Company-wide

[00:00] Evelyn Park: Hey everyone, good morning, good afternoon, wherever you are. Uh, welcome to the June all-hands. We're gonna keep this to about an hour, lots to cover but try to leave time for questions. Quick housekeeping: slides are in the #all-hands channel, recording will be posted.

[00:22] Evelyn Park: Quick top line — Q2 is shaping up well. We closed three Dedicated deals last month, two of which are enterprise with multi-region needs, and we're seeing a steady uptick in trial-to-paid conversion for hosted API on mid-market accounts. Revenue is up vs plan — not epically over plan but healthy and real.

[01:05] Marcus Li: Yeah just to add, from infra perspective we've shipped the new kernel selection logic and a set of attention optimizations that's meaningfully reduced p95 for long-context inferencing. So for a 8k token workload we're seeing p95 drop by roughly 18-22% in our test clusters. There's still work on batching heuristics and memory layout.

[01:45] Audience (applause emoji in chat)

[02:00] Priya Nair: On the engineering side, we've been focusing on stability for Dedicated — the autoscaler changes and the burst capacity paths are out in staging and early canaries. There was a regression with kv cash eviction (note: transcription shows 'KV cash' in the logs) that Mateo and the SRE team fixed last week.

[02:35] Mateo Alvarez: Yep that was a weird one — turned out to be a GC/internals interplay on the GPU memory manager. We added more guardrails and better observability in the runtime, so ops will see clearer signs before it impacts rollouts.

[03:10] Daniel Ruiz: Product updates — Redwood Console v3 is rolling to prod next week. The big thing here: token-level cost breakdowns, per-route latency histograms, and an auto-suggest for batching and cache configs based on traffic patterns. We'll demo some of the Console dashboards in the next townhall for sales and solutions.

[03:45] Sophie Chen: On growth, enterprise demand is getting more sophisticated — customers are asking about Private (V-P-C) deployment, KMS integrations, and the audit trail. Our renewals are doing okay, but we need better packaged security artifacts to accelerate sales cycles. We'll work with security to make a short 'enterprise pack' for AE handoff.

[04:20] Evelyn Park: Security — quick update, SOC 2 Type II is in flight, we've completed the readiness assessment and are scheduling evidence collection next week. Also, we added a new optional HSM/KMS integration for Private customers — still early, but it's in alpha with one pilot.

[05:00] Someone (unlabeled): Question in chat — are we doing a price change for Dedicated?

[05:12] Daniel Ruiz: Not a blunt price change, more of a phased rollout: clearer tiers, burst pricing, and a reserved commit discount. The goal is to make unit economics predictable for customers while protecting margin. I'll share specifics in the product doc and we'll circulate to sales.

[05:45] Evelyn Park: Hiring/org — Lina?

[05:50] Lina Kaur: Quick updates: hiring pace is up — we're focusing on infra, core runtime, and two roles for solutions engineering. We also piloted a manager training series and an IC career ladder — feedback was positive; we'll iterate and then roll it out company-wide by end of month. Also please submit flight requests early for Q3 team retreats.

[06:20] Evelyn Park: Good. A couple of strategic notes — first, we're doubling down on 'serving' as our core thesis: not owning models but the best way to serve them at scale. So think in product decisions about predictability and economics for the customer. Second, reliability and graceful degradation — automatic fallbacks to model variants and cross-region routing — this is what will keep enterprise customers live during incidents.

[07:05] Marcus Li: Small tech demo — I won't screen share the whole thing but we ran a benchmark on the new kernel versus baseline for Llama-2-Chat style loads; the new kernel gives consistent perf wins at longer contexts and is slightly more memory-efficient when quantized. There's a caveat: certain microarchitectures see less benefit, so we need per-hardware profiles. We'll publish the benchmark sheet.

[07:50] Priya Nair: On scaling — the autoscaler now supports scheduled capacity reservations which helps predictable batch loads, and we've added a safety cap to avoid noisy neighbor spikes in shared clusters. This is important for Hosted customers and also for Dedicated where we want isolation.

[08:25] Evelyn Park: Questions — we have about 35 minutes for Q&A, please use the raise hand or the Q&A tab.

[08:40] Staff Q: From Sales — what materials do we have to support security questions during discovery?

[08:50] Sophie Chen: We're creating an enterprise bundle with SOC 2 readiness docs, a tech brief on Private deployment (networking checklist: VPC, subnets, routes, NAT, etc.), and a short one-pager on encryption/KMS. Security will help review.

[09:15] Security Rep (unlabeled): We'll add a standard controls matrix and a sample audit log extract so customers can see what the data flow looks like. Also note: evidence collection for SOC 2 will need a few product owners to pull artifacts — we'll reach out after this meeting.

[09:45] Staff Q: Are we planning any changes to the hosted API pricing?

[09:50] Daniel Ruiz: No immediate changes for hosted API pricing, we continue to optimize unit costs and recommend quantization/Optimize suggestions per workload. Any upsell around Dedicated will be through clearer reserve tiers.

[10:20] Staff Q: On the kernel — will this require downtime for Dedicated customers to upgrade?

[10:30] Marcus Li: It should be seamless; upgrades happen per node with canaries and fallback. There may be transient cold-start differences but we have rollback paths. We'll coordinate with Customer Success for any customers in pilot.

[11:00] Evelyn Park: Quick shoutout — Engineering and SRE for reliability fixes last week, and Sales for closing the two multi-region deals. Great cross-functional work.

[11:20] Mateo Alvarez: One operational note — we observed a small regression in metrics ingestion pipeline when the Console rollouts hit a large tenant; ops mitigated it and we're adding backpressure to the pipeline.

[11:45] Staff Q: When will we open the sign-up for private on-prem pilot?

[11:55] Daniel Ruiz: We're targeting mid-July for a limited on-prem pilot with two customers under NDA. The VPC offering is already in alpha with a partner. We'll share the requirements and checklist.

[12:20] Evelyn Park: Ok, last few items — FYI leadership will host small roundtables next week on Q3 priorities. If you're an IC and have strong opinions about product direction, please sign up. Also managers please prioritize the manager training feedback.

[12:50] Evelyn Park: Alright thank you everyone — we'll post the deck and recording. See the action items in the notes. Meeting adjourned.

[13:05] (meeting end)

Notes: Transcript contains occasional transcription errors (e.g., 'KV cash' for KV cache, 'SOC two' for SOC 2, 'V-P-C' spelled out), and some speaker attributions are generalized for company-wide portions.
